name: Chez Damier
hook: A Chicago dancer at the Warehouse who moved to Detroit, co-ran the club where the two scenes' DJs shared a booth, and worked Kevin Saunderson's A&R desk before starting his own label.

blurb.age7: Chez Damier danced to Frankie Knuckles' music as a kid in Chicago, then moved to Detroit and helped run a club and a record label before starting his own.
blurb.age13: Chez Damier grew up dancing at Frankie Knuckles' Warehouse in Chicago, then moved to Detroit in the 1980s. In 1988 he co-owned the Music Institute, a short-lived club where Detroit techno and Chicago house DJs, including Derrick May and Kevin Saunderson, played the same room. He also worked A&R for Saunderson's label KMS, releasing his own record 'Can You Feel It' there in 1992, before co-founding Prescription Records with Ron Trent in 1993.
blurb.adult: Damier is one of the clearest bridge figures between Chicago house and Detroit techno on this map: a Chicago dancer who relocated and became, for eighteen months, co-owner of the one club where both cities' DJs shared a booth. His run at KMS, first as Saunderson's A&R, then as a released artist with 'Can You Feel It' (1992), sits ahead of Prescription Records, the label he and Ron Trent started in 1993 that helped define 1990s deep house.
